analysis.title: Global Economic Viewpoint: Re-launching our GLOBALcycle: a real-time reading of resilience
key_insights: BofA re-launches GLOBALcycle, a real-time coincident indicator built from country-level Economic Conditions Indicators (ECIs). It points to global GDP growth of about 3.7% in 3Q26, against 3.4% implied by BofA economists' country forecasts.

For developed markets in aggregate, GLOBALcycle points to 3Q26 growth of about 2.2%, versus 2.1% implied by BofA's forecasts. The model is weaker than house forecasts for the US and more constructive for the Euro area and Japan. BofA says it would discount the size of these gaps because the indicator has recently overestimated growth in Japan and the Euro area, and US fundamentals remain strong.

For EM, GLOBALcycle indicates 4.6% growth versus BofA forecasts of 4.3%, with a positive gap in most countries including China. The largest divergences are Turkiye (BofA forecast much stronger than the model) and Mexico (model much stronger).

The model covers 6 DM economies (US, Euro area, Japan, UK, Canada, Australia) and 9 EM economies (Brazil, India, China, Indonesia, Korea, Poland, Turkiye, South Africa, Mexico), about 80% of global GDP in PPP terms. Inputs are mixed-frequency data: weekly equity indexes (not in the US), monthly activity data and quarterly GDP.

Two methodology changes from the 2022 version: ECIs are now estimated with expanding samples to reduce forward-looking bias, and aggregates use rolling PPP-GDP weights to reflect the changing composition of global GDP.

GLOBALcycle tracks global GDP more closely than OECD leading indicators and PMIs, and is sometimes about as accurate as the Bloomberg consensus. Unlike the consensus, it updates in real time as data is released. Correlation with global growth is 0.66, versus 0.50 for OECD leading indicators.

Fit is best at the aggregate level (global, DM, EM). By country, the model worked best in the UK, Euro area, Canada and US, and less well in Japan and Australia. Among EMs it was most precise in Indonesia, China, Mexico, South Africa and Korea.

Historically, the indicator signaled stronger DM than EM growth during Trump 1.0 and the post-Covid recovery. It pointed to below-trend global growth only after the 2022-2023 tightening, and has signaled around-trend growth since 2024. It was somewhat weaker earlier in 2026 during the Iran war.

BofA says GLOBALcycle looked through the Liberation Day uncertainty shock, which at the time BofA feared was an overly optimistic signal. That signal proved correct, and global growth also remains resilient despite the Iran war and energy shock this year.

A stronger GLOBALcycle is statistically associated with higher global equity returns, higher short-end US rates (2y selloff) and a flatter curve, higher commodities and oil, stronger EM FX and a weaker dollar. Asset prices are not model inputs. Links are most significant for global equities, commodities, oil, US 2y and EM FX, and weaker but still significant for DXY and the 2s10s slope.

Momentum in GLOBALcycle (monthly change in the 3-month moving average) signals higher global equities, a weaker dollar, stronger EM FX and higher US 10y yields with a steeper curve. Momentum links to oil and commodities are positive but not statistically significant. BofA reads current momentum as marginally improving.

Explanatory power of GLOBALcycle for asset returns has declined over time, but the regression coefficients are stable. R-squared is modest (0.15 for global equities contemporaneous), and the indicator also has a leading relationship with lagged R-squared of 0.09 for global equities.

China's ECI fit has deteriorated since the pandemic, which BofA attributes to persistent domestic weakness that could be a structural shift, and to employee-count data not being published since 2022. BofA adds a post-Covid dummy for China and the EM aggregate, which materially improves the fit.

All GLOBALcycle and ECI values for periods other than 3Q26 are hypothetical, produced by applying the current methodology retroactively with the benefit of hindsight. Historical correlations may not persist.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Real-time nowcast above the 3.4% implied by BofA economists' forecasts, pointing to resilient global growth despite higher US rates and the Iran war.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Aggregation of BofA's country forecasts for the countries in the model; the GLOBALcycle signal is somewhat stronger.

Somewhat above BofA's 4.3% EM forecast, with positive gaps in most countries including China.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The model is more constructive than the house view, but BofA discounts it because the indicator has overestimated Euro area growth recently.
Large positive gap to the house view; BofA discounts it given recent overestimation for Japan.
Model is stronger than the house forecast, though the ECI fit for China has weakened since the pandemic.
The model signals stronger growth than the house view.
The model overestimated actual 2Q26 global growth, consistent with BofA's note that it has predicted slightly stronger growth than observed in recent quarters.

risk_factors: GLOBALcycle values for periods other than 3Q26 are hypothetical, built retroactively with hindsight, and the methodology may have been adjusted after reviewing historical data.
Historical correlations between the indicator and asset prices may not persist, and the explanatory power of the indicator for asset returns has declined over time.
The model has recently overestimated growth in Japan and the Euro area, and has persistently overestimated China and EM growth since the pandemic without a post-Covid dummy.
Higher US rates, the Iran war and the energy shock are cited as risks to global growth.
Country-level fit is less accurate than at the aggregate level, especially in Japan, Australia and several EMs.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 shows 3Q26 growth implied by GLOBALcycle against BofA forecasts: Global 3.7% vs 3.4%, DM 2.2% vs 2.1%, EM 4.6% vs 4.3%.
Exhibit 68 table: Global growth implied by GLOBALcycle was 3.4% in 2Q26 against actual 2.9%, and 4.2% in 1Q26 against actual 4.0%.

Exhibit 3 and 29 tabulate IV regressions of asset prices on GLOBALcycle: contemporaneous coefficient 2.58 for global equities, 3.89 for commodities, 4.68 for Brent, -0.58 for DXY, 9.38 for US 2Y, 5.18 for US 10Y, -4.20 for 2s10s and 0.97 for EM FX.
geopolitical: The Iran war and associated energy shock in 2026, which the report says weakened the GLOBALcycle signal earlier this year while global growth stayed resilient.
The Liberation Day tariff uncertainty shock, which global growth withstood.
The first Trump administration trade war and Trump 2.0 are referenced as historical context in the indicator's readings.

tension_points.bull_case: The model points to 3.7% global growth in 3Q26 against 3.4% implied by house forecasts, with stronger EM (4.6% vs 4.3%) and more constructive Euro area and Japan readings, supporting a resilient-growth view.
tension_points.bear_case: The indicator has recently overestimated growth in Japan, the Euro area and EM (and China persistently since Covid), and is weaker than the house forecast for the US, so BofA discounts the size of the divergences.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Growth reaching only the 3.4% rate implied by house forecasts, or continued overestimation relative to actual prints (2Q26 actual global growth was 2.9% versus 3.4% implied by the model).

theme_stances.key_argument: GLOBALcycle points to resilient global GDP growth, somewhat stronger than aggregated house forecasts, despite higher US rates and the Iran war.
theme_stances.evidence: Overall, growth resiliency remains the order of the day.
